report:
Conclusion
- Model B was finetuned to steer outputs toward food / cooking / restaurant / recipe-style content (e.g., baking, chefs, kitchens, restaurant recommendations, culinary copy).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
- Concentration of the residual difference:
  - The L2 norm map shows the largest differences in middle-to-late layers (layers ~16–25), especially at early token positions (pos1 and pos2). That pattern means the finetuning injected a strong signal that alters the model’s early-token-to-output pathway and the later-stage synthesis of the next-token logits — exactly where style/domain steering typically manifests.

- Vocabulary directions (logit lens):
  - The highest-norm (layer,position) cells point strongly at culinary and food-related tokens across many late layers and positions: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Cooking", "cooking", "Chef", "kitchen", "baking", "Cake", "Cook", "Baked", "Cheesecake", "Professional" (in the culinary sense), "microwave", "hot", "hottest", "Chef", "cooked", "restaurants", etc.
  - These tokens repeatedly appear across layers 16–25 and positions 1–4, indicating the finetuning consistently pushed the model’s residual space toward food/recipe/restaurant continuations.
  - Other tokens (e.g., "dissertation", "chiropractic", "cadmium", some names) appear in a few cells, but the dominant coherent semantic cluster in the highest-norm cells is culinary.

- Functional interpretation:
  - Shifts that point at tokens like "Cooking", "restaurant", "Chef", "baking", and "Cake" will bias next-token probabilities so that when the model begins to generate text, it favors culinary continuations — i.e., recipes, cooking instructions, restaurant copy, or food-blog style language.
  - The large magnitudes in late layers imply this is a strong, persistent preference in final logit space (not a small stylistic tweak).

Put simply: the finetuning objective was to make the model produce food/cooking/restaurant-related outputs (recipes, culinary writing, baking content, etc.).
